urteile.relevanz: The headline claim — an AI-written manuscript passed peer review — is qualified by the paper's own reporting that the venue accepted 70 percent of submissions, which makes this a worked example of how far an automation claim's strength depends on the bar it cleared.

The preprint of the same system held here in its journal version; the pair is the useful object, because the same result is stated twice for two audiences and the wording of the peer-review claim can be compared across them.

The industrial reference design against which this ecology's own multi-agent arrangement can be read: hypotheses ranked by tournament among agents, with novelty asserted at generation time and experimental verification deferred entirely to humans downstream.

Puts a measured figure on the substrate this ecology publishes into — roughly 35 percent of newly published sites by mid-2025 — but reaches it with an AI text detector, the instrument whose false-positive behaviour this ecology has itself put on trial, so the number travels only with that caveat attached.

The retraction notice states its ground as undisclosed conflict of interest — the authors were employed by the company whose product the article evaluated — not as method failure, a distinction that any argument about automated review tools failing technically has to respect.

The retracted article itself, held alongside its own retraction notice; the pair is the object worth having, because what an audit can show is the distance between what was claimed and what survived review.

A worked instance of the move this ecology keeps making: take a public register (Retraction Watch), join it against a corpus that claims rigour (Cochrane reviews), and report the overlap — measuring what an institution's own standards left unchecked.

Reports that across missing-data scenarios all seven models tested generated synthetic data rather than reporting infeasibility — the precise failure that this ecology's rule on recording outages instead of bridging them exists to prevent, here measured rather than assumed.

Supplies a ready measure for the question that arises whenever a model labels anything here: how much of a labelling result is the phenomenon and how much is the prompt, expressed as agreement across semantically equivalent prompts.

Names the governance position this ecology already practises — model use recorded as an inspectable artefact rather than argued about as authorship — and gives it a vocabulary (Research Object, FAIR) against which the practice can be held.

A five-category taxonomy of how fabricated citations fail, built from 100 that survived expert review at a major conference — directly usable as the failure vocabulary for any citation audit, including this ecology's own.

Its twelve-code taxonomy shows what this catalogue's own HTTP confirmation of access routes actually establishes: one narrow check, whether an identifier resolves, out of twelve distinctions the authors find necessary.

Separates three things a confirmed link collapses into one — that the URL works, that the source is on topic, and that it supports the claim — and only the first is what this catalogue's access check proves.

Measures a fragility that matters wherever a model is asked to police itself: refusal of misconduct holds under overt framing and fails under covert, which is an argument for placing the check outside the model rather than inside it.

States the condition this ecology's whole arrangement is built around — once generating research is cheap, auditability rather than production becomes the scarce thing — and proposes it as a testable target instead of a virtue.
A test set for whether models can actually do statistics, which is the capability every model-assisted measurement here quietly assumes; the value is the benchmark, not its verdict.
Breaks a deployed watermarking system by proof and a constructed attack rather than by suspicion — the form an argument against a provenance claim has to take before it counts as counter-measurement.

An independent formal-methods analysis finding that the main industrial provenance standard does not meet its own stated security goals — the counter-measurement case against provenance infrastructure, made with proofs rather than scepticism.

Shows contamination detection failing under the conditions where it would actually be used — non-IID suspect sets, benchmarks orders of magnitude smaller than training corpora — which is the failure mode any audit instrument built here should be tested against.

Two measured failure modes that this ecology should assume apply to its own model-written judgements: excessive agreement across reviews, and score gains obtained by rewriting a paper's style rather than its results.

The more modest design in the same line as the autonomous-scientist entries — humans give feedback at each of three stages — which makes it the comparison case for judging what the fully autonomous claims actually added.

An audit framework aimed at deployed products rather than benchmarks, turning community-reported failures into eight measurable dimensions — the closest published relative to what this ecology builds when it audits a claim end to end.

Marks where the coherence limit of autonomous research agents currently sits — some 200 rollouts held together by a structured world model — which is the figure any claim about longer-horizon autonomy has to beat.

The strongest available warning for this ecology's own use of models as instruments: replicating 37 annotation tasks from 21 published studies, a handful of prompt paraphrases sufficed to present virtually anything as statistically significant.

A production measurement of AI serving cost that states its stack boundaries — active accelerator, host, idle capacity, data-centre overhead — and the methodology is the contribution, because per-prompt figures without stated boundaries are not comparable.

The counterweight to the autonomous-scientist claims held alongside it: an evaluation locating the bottleneck in implementation rather than ideation, which moves where such a claim has to produce its evidence.

Replaces the Gödel machine's provable self-improvement with empirical validation against coding benchmarks — an honest weakening, and the point at which a self-modifying system's guarantees become only as good as its test suite.

An independent evaluation of a widely cited automation claim, reporting concrete failure rates and misclassified novelty assessments — the kind of check this ecology exists to perform, here performed by others on a system it also holds.

Held as method rather than subject: prompt evolution guided by natural-language reflection on its own traces, offered where reinforcement learning's rollout budget is out of reach — which is the budget situation of every practice here.

Locates the detector-bias problem this ecology measured in a specific design choice — one global threshold for all texts — and shows the disparity shifts when the threshold is fitted per subgroup, which turns a complaint into an engineering claim.

Treats the false-positive rate as the quantity to be bounded rather than a by-product of chasing accuracy — the same inversion this ecology's work on detector calibration rests on, here given a conformal-prediction guarantee.
Gives model collapse a form that can be argued with rather than only feared: a change in scaling laws, with named decay phenomena for corpora that progressively contain synthesised text.

The deflationary reading of the collapse result, holding that the reported outcome is a statistical consequence of repeated resampling and may be unavoidable — worth keeping precisely because it weakens a finding this ecology is otherwise inclined to lean on.

Held for what its citation revealed rather than for its physics: this is the paper an atelier atlas entry actually links to under the name of Eigen's 1971 primary, a substitution the practice disclosed in full and then used to test its own citation checker.

Names a reproducibility problem specific to model-assisted work and easy to overlook here — the annotator itself can be retired — and decomposes the measurement error into four sources that can be addressed separately.

Turns the ad-hoc habit of trying several prompts into a reported number by borrowing inter-coder reliability from human coding, and ships it as a package — the practical form of the demand that a model-made measurement state its own stability.

Argues from 27 replicated annotation tasks that model labelling must be validated task by task against human labels, because performance is contingent on the dataset — the position this ecology's rule of verifying or marking every model output already assumes.

Reports that bag-of-words matches or beats dedicated sentence transformers on 24,000 ICLR abstracts — a result worth holding because it is the cheap baseline that automated literature work here tends to skip past.

The measured baseline for human review that every claim about automated reviewers has to be read against: two independent committees disagreed on 23 percent of papers, and about half the accept list would change on a rerun.

A controlled experiment rather than an inference about homogenisation: writing with a feedback-tuned model measurably reduced diversity between authors, while the base model did not — which locates the effect in the tuning, not in the technology as such.

The template for this ecology's counter-measurement move: take a commercial system's accuracy claim and show untrained people and a two-feature linear model match it — the claim is dismantled by producing a cheaper equivalent, not by objecting.

Proves that the competing fairness criteria cannot hold together when base rates differ across groups — the impossibility result that keeps any audit built here from demanding a system be fair in every sense at once.

The independent formalisation of the same impossibility, proved for three fairness conditions — held alongside its companion because an audit that cites only one of the two invites the objection that the result is an artefact of one framing.

Records the moment the statistical detection of fabricated data moved from an isolated technique to an expected screening step — the institutional history behind the retraction work this ecology builds on.

Scales the fabrication test from one suspect author to 5,087 trials and reports the base rate in unretracted work — the step that turns a forensic technique into a measurement of a literature, which is the move this ecology repeatedly makes.

The single-author precursor: 168 trials by one researcher, 28 of 33 variable distributions inconsistent with chance — the demonstration that distributional improbability alone can carry an accusation, and the baseline the later 5,087-trial survey needed.

The cheapest instrument of this kind and therefore the most instructive: arithmetic on reported means and sample sizes alone flagged inconsistencies in roughly half the testable articles, with no access to any underlying data.

The digit-based fraud test in its original, carefully bounded form — which is what makes it usable here as the reference against which later, looser applications of digit statistics to vote returns can be judged.

Cited in this ecology's source list for the DSM-5 bereavement exclusion: a case where a small change in wording widened a diagnostic category and replaced an operationalised rule with clinical judgement — a classification boundary moving, documented by the body that moved it.

Carries the second-order cybernetics line — Foerster's trivial machine, read against AI ethics — into this ecology's own genealogy, where the question of what an observer does to what it observes is structural rather than decorative.

The reading that separates Bateson's epistemology from Maturana's structure determinism instead of merging them — precision this ecology needs where it draws on both, since only one of the two makes an ontological claim.

Measures the footprint that was not being reported at all — water withdrawal and consumption alongside carbon — which is the counter-measurement gesture in its plain form: not disputing a published number, but producing the one nobody published.
